verdict: Lead volume dropped sharply this week; cost per lead and attribution need immediate repair.
narrative: In the last 28 days, you received 23 leads at an average cost of $166 per lead — and over the most recent 7 days, lead volume fell 71% while spend rose 9%, pushing cost per lead up roughly 280% week-over-week. At the same time, your CRM recorded 109 new opportunities this period against only 23 platform-reported leads, which means a significant number of contacts are not being tied back to their paid source and the cost-per-lead figure as reported cannot be taken at face value. We are closing that tracking gap now so that every contact is properly attributed before next week's report. In parallel, ad targeting and creative are being reviewed to address the efficiency decline; you should expect a clearer, more accurate lead count as the attribution repair takes effect.

highlights.phrase: leads received from paid channels in the last 28 days
average cost per lead this period — overstated until attribution is repaired
new opportunities recorded in your CRM this period, well above platform-reported leads

watch_item.issue: A major gap between CRM contacts (109) and platform-reported leads (23) means cost per lead is unreliable and roughly 86 contacts have no tracked paid source.
watch_item.fix: Conversion tracking is being repaired this week to reconcile all contacts to their source channels, restoring accurate reporting.
